summary: The guard workflow gets cost controls that may only make a run cheaper without changing what a gate proves, declared in ci/jobs.json and enforced by the read-only CI contract verifier: superseded pull request runs are cancelled by a concurrency group, the reviewed NuGet packages are cached in the heavy jobs with a key derived from the reviewed lock files, and the re-validation schedule moves from weekly to monthly. The base additionally classifies the verified changed set with trusted-base/Get-IFXChangeScope.ps1, which the workflow reaches through Invoke-IFXTrustedBase.ps1 -Mode Scope so that the workflow references only scripts the base already owns, in a step that is continue-on-error so a base that cannot classify, or any failure, leads to a full run: with an explicit head, scope records-and-plans means every changed path between the verified merge base and that head is a formal plan document, an authorization record or a decision record, and every other outcome, including an empty changed set or a failure, is full. On records-and-plans, the workflow skips the head candidate steps of v3-architecture and both v3-cross-platform legs, and the trusted base runner records guardrails as skipped for v3-architecture, the three quality checks and v3-specialized-database, which inherit the verdict their unchanged inputs already have at the base. v3-pre-diff, Validate, Pre, HistoricalIntegrity and the G03, G04, G05 and Plan04 gates always run. The 13 required check names, the job DAG, the trigger semantics, the ruleset and the strict up-to-date policy stay unchanged, and no gate becomes conditional at job level.
rationale: Measured on 2026-09-17, one pull request run costs 73 to 75 billable Actions minutes on this private repository: 30 for the Windows leg at the 2x rate, 13 for v3-architecture, 10 for the Ubuntu leg, 6 for the solution quality gate and 5 for the database gate, with almost all of it in .NET restore, build and test steps. At 2700 of 3000 minutes used, the remaining plan of roughly 19 to 23 runs does not fit in one monthly budget. Cancelling superseded runs, caching the reviewed packages and running the schedule monthly reduce cost with no effect on any verdict. The change scope classification is the larger saving because about half of the pull requests of this plan add or revoke authorization records and plan documents only; those paths are review artifacts of this package and are not inputs of the architecture, quality or database gates, whose inputs were already verified at the base, which the strict up-to-date ruleset keeps current. Classification is base-owned, reads head only as Git objects, is bound to the base protection configuration and fails closed to a full run, so a head cannot claim a cheaper scope for itself. Trimming the Windows leg was measured and rejected: its time is spent in exactly the platform-sensitive scripts. Classification is reached through the runner because the manifest check requires every script the workflow names to exist in the base package, so a workflow that named a new script directly could not be introduced together with that script. The user asked for CI cost reduction on 2026-09-18 and chose to do this optimization before continuing Plan 06 work. Refines D19 and the activation contract of D10.
